To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a CMOS ASIC was designed and fabricated to generate arbitrary, high-speed, dynamic phase patterns, which were applied in acoustic hologram applications to demonstrate acoustic pressure mapping and particle trapping and to drive a PMUT array.
we have demonstrated an integrated circuit for generating dynamic acoustic holograms, which can be used to control acoustic fields for particle manipulation.
a multi-channel signal generator ASIC has been developed to drive acoustic holograms, and the performance and flexibility of the ASIC have been verified with experimental results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an integrated CMOS ASIC for the generation of arbitrary, dynamic phase control of acoustic waves for acoustic hologram and particle manipulation applications.
the development of a multi-channel signal generator ASIC to drive an array of acoustic sources for hologram applications.
the design, fabrication, and characterization of a CMOS ASIC that can be used to drive a transducer array in order to create acoustic holograms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this ASIC is capable of generating arbitrary, dynamic phase holograms for ultrasonic manipulation of particles.

this paper presents an ASIC that has a footprint of <inline-formula><tex-math notation = "LaTeX">$117.5 \times 8.8 \,\,\mu m^2$</tex-math></formula>, which generates 16-level phase patterns at a 8 MHz output frequency.
this ASIC is a good starting point to develop an integrated acoustic hologram system with CMOS and PMU transducers, with a view to miniaturization and cost reduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a CMOS signal generator ASIC has been successfully developed to generate arbitrary and dynamic phase patterns for ultrasonic applications.
a multi-channel, high-speed, high-resolution, and compact signal generator has been successfully developed for acoustic hologram generation.
we have designed and demonstrated a multi-channel, programmable, and reconfigurable ASIC to drive acoustic holograms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single ASIC can drive a large array of PMUTs with a high degree of flexibility.
the developed ASIC can be used to control a large number of transducers in an acoustic hologram system and can be used as a platform for the development of future integrated systems.
the developed CMOS ASIC can be used as an enabling technology to drive the development of a new generation of ultrasonic transducers for a variety of applications.
